prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1456; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On the afternoon in question, Driver 1 was completing a left turn at a Pearland, Texas intersection when the front of Driver 2's vehicle made contact with the rear quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat and was present in the vehicle at the time of the impact, as confirmed by both drivers and by the witnesses on scene. Driver 2 gave a statement that matched Driver 1's account of how the collision occurred. Two witnesses and the scene photographs are consistent with that sequence. The visible damage to the rear quarter panel and bumper corresponds to the impact described, and no earlier damage to Driver 1's vehicle was known to any party. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and described significant pain. The impact appeared light, and the severity of the reported injury does not fit the force observed at the scene. Driver 1 is named on the auto policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene.
